title: feat(security): add rate limiting and lockout for failed authentication
description: Anyone can send unlimited requests, including guesses against identities. Add rate limiting so brute force attacks are slow and visible.
requirements: Limit requests per IP and, for authenticated routes, per account address
Count failed token checks separately and apply a stricter limit
Return `429` with a JSON `{ "error": ... }` body and a `Retry-After` header
Limits are configurable by environment variables with safe defaults, and documented in `.env.example`
`/healthz` is never limited
execution: Look at the `@fastify/rate-limit` plugin and wire it in `src/api/server.ts`. Keep the limiter behind a small interface so a shared store (for example Redis) can be added later.
tests: Add tests in `test/api.test.ts` for the limit being hit, the header, and `/healthz` staying open. Commit: `feat(security): add rate limiting`.

title: feat(store): add a PostgreSQL account store
description: SQLite is fine for one server but not for teams that need a managed database. Add a Postgres implementation of `AccountStore`.
requirements: Implement `PostgresStore` in `src/store/postgres.ts` against the `AccountStore` interface
Add a migration for the `accounts` and `identity_methods` tables (same shape as `SqliteStore`)
`STORE=postgres` and `DATABASE_URL` select it in `src/config.ts` and `src/index.ts`
Concurrent `create` calls for the same address must produce exactly one success and one `AccountExistsError`
`listAccessible` must use an index and respect the `after` cursor and `limit`
execution: Use the `pg` package. Reuse `methodKey` from `src/store/access.ts` so lookups match the other stores.
tests: Add `PostgresStore` to the factories in `test/store.test.ts` so it must pass the same contract tests. Skip it cleanly when no database is available. Commit: `feat(store): add postgres store`.

title: feat(keys): add a CLI to rotate signing keys
description: `AccountService.rotateSigningKey` exists but nothing calls it. Operators need a command to rotate keys on a schedule.
requirements: Add `npm run rotate -- --older-than 90d [--dry-run]`
For each account whose newest key is older than the limit, add a new key and keep the old keys
Print how many accounts were rotated and never print secrets
Safe to run twice: accounts already rotated are skipped
Document the command and why old keys are kept (wallets may not have switched yet)
execution: Add `src/cli/rotate.ts` using `loadConfig`, the store and `AccountService`. You may need a `listAll` or an iterator on `AccountStore`; add it to every store.
tests: Test with the memory store: old key rotated, new key skipped, dry run changes nothing. Commit: `feat(keys): add rotation cli`.

title: feat(keys): support KMS envelope encryption through a pluggable interface
description: Today one `KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY` from the environment encrypts every signing key. Operators with a cloud KMS or Vault want the master key to stay outside the process.
requirements: Introduce a `KeyEncryptor` interface (encrypt and decrypt of a data key) and make `KeyStore` use it
Keep the current local-key behaviour as the default implementation, with no change to stored data
Add one reference implementation for a KMS of your choice, behind an optional dependency
Store the wrapped data key with each record using a new format version (`v2`), and still read `v1`
Document the threat model: what this protects against and what it does not
execution: Start with the interface and a refactor that keeps all current tests green, then add the KMS implementation in a separate commit.
tests: Existing `test/keystore.test.ts` must pass unchanged. Add tests for `v1` to `v2` reading and for a failing KMS. Commit: `feat(keys): add key encryptor interface`.

title: feat(auth): add an email one-time-code identity provider
description: SEP-30 servers accept tokens from an identity provider the operator trusts. Lumenward verifies them but ships no provider. Add a small reference provider for email codes.
requirements: A separate small service under `providers/email-otp` with `POST /start` (send a code) and `POST /verify` (return a signed JWT)
The JWT carries the OpenID Connect claims `email` and `email_verified: true` and is signed with an asymmetric key
Codes expire in 10 minutes, are single use, and are rate limited
Email sending goes through an interface with a console implementation for development
README section showing how to point `EXTERNAL_JWKS` at it
execution: Reuse `jose` for signing. Do not store codes in plain text.
tests: Tests for expiry, single use, wrong code, and a token that Lumenward's `externalPrincipal` accepts. Commit: `feat(auth): add email otp provider`.

title: feat(auth): add an SMS one-time-code identity provider with a pluggable gateway
description: Many users have a phone number but no email. Add a reference provider that issues tokens with a verified `phone_number`.
requirements: A service under `providers/sms-otp` with the same start and verify flow as the email provider
Phone numbers are validated as E.164, matching `src/service/validation.ts`
The SMS gateway is an interface. Ship a console implementation and one real gateway example
Limit attempts per number and per IP
The token carries `phone_number` and `phone_number_verified: true`
execution: Share the code and token logic with the email provider instead of copying it. Consider a small shared package.
tests: Tests for invalid numbers, expiry, attempt limits, and acceptance by `externalPrincipal`. Commit: `feat(auth): add sms otp provider`.

title: feat(ops): add an append-only audit log
description: Operators need to know who registered, changed, deleted or asked for a signature, and when. Today nothing is recorded.
requirements: Record register, update, delete, list and sign events with time, account address, which identity matched, and the result
Never record tokens, secrets, signatures or full transactions. Record the transaction hash only
Store events in a table that the service can only append to
Add `npm run audit-log -- --since 2026-01-01` to export events as JSON lines
Failures of the audit log must not allow a signature to be returned without a record
execution: Add an `AuditLog` interface next to `AccountStore` and call it from `AccountService`. Decide and document what happens when logging fails.
tests: Tests that every API action produces one event and that no event contains secrets. Commit: `feat(ops): add audit log`.

title: feat(ops): add an opt-in Prometheus metrics endpoint
description: Operators cannot see request rates, failures or signing volume.
requirements: `GET /metrics` in Prometheus text format, off unless `METRICS_ENABLED=true`
Counters for requests by route and status, signing requests, and auth failures
A histogram of request duration
No account addresses, emails or phone numbers in any label
Can be bound to a separate port so it is not exposed with the public API
execution: The `prom-client` package works well here.
tests: Test that metrics are off by default, appear when enabled, and contain no personal data. Commit: `feat(ops): add metrics`.

title: test: add a black-box SEP-30 conformance suite
description: Today tests call the server in process. A separate suite that talks HTTP to any base URL would let wallet teams check any SEP-30 server, including this one.
requirements: A command `npm run conformance -- --url https://... --sep10-token ...` that runs a series of checks
Cover all six endpoints: success paths, `400`, `401`, `404` and `409` cases from the SEP-30 text
Check that auth methods are never returned and that `authenticated` appears only on matched identities
Check that signers are listed newest first
Print a pass or fail report and exit non-zero on failure
execution: Read the [SEP-30 text](https://github.com/stellar/stellar-protocol/blob/master/ecosystem/sep-0030.md) first and quote the rule each check comes from in a comment.
tests: Run the suite against Lumenward in CI. Commit: `test: add sep-30 conformance suite`.

title: test: add a two-server recovery integration test
description: The core promise is that two independent servers recover an account together. No test proves it end to end.
requirements: Start two Lumenward instances with different keys and databases (for example with `docker-compose.yml`)
On Stellar testnet, create an account, register it on both servers and add both signing keys with thresholds so neither can act alone
Run a recovery that adds a new signer using both signatures
Assert that a transaction signed by only one server is rejected by the network
Run the test in CI on demand, and document how to run it locally
execution: The official TypeScript wallet SDK supports SEP-30 and can be used for the client side. Check its current docs before pinning a version.
tests: The test itself is the deliverable. Commit: `test: add two-server recovery test`.

title: feat(audit): add an audit GitHub Action
description: The recovery set auditor is a command line tool. Teams want it to run on a schedule and fail a workflow when an account is misconfigured.
requirements: A composite or Node action in `action/` that wraps `lumenward-audit`
Inputs: `account`, `recovery-keys`, `horizon-url`
Fail the job on critical findings and print all findings in the job summary
Example workflow in the README
Document how to run it on a schedule
execution: Reuse `auditAccount` directly instead of spawning the CLI if you write a Node action.
tests: Test the action logic with fixtures like `test/auditor.test.ts`. Commit: `feat(audit): add github action`.

title: feat(audit): read recovery keys from a running Lumenward server
description: Today you must copy each server's signing key by hand into `--recovery-key`. The server already returns them from `GET /accounts/<address>`.
requirements: Add `--server <url> --server-token <jwt>` (repeatable) to `lumenward-audit`
Fetch each server's signer list for the account and use the newest key from each as the recovery key
Report if two servers return the same key (a shared-key finding)
Report servers that do not know the account
Never print tokens
execution: Extend `src/cli/audit.ts`. Keep the pure checks in `src/audit/auditor.ts`.
tests: Use a local fake HTTP server in tests. Commit: `feat(audit): read keys from servers`.

title: feat(signing): add a configurable operation allow list
description: Today the server signs any operation as long as the sources are allowed. A recovery server only needs a few operation types, for example `setOptions`. Limiting them reduces damage if an identity is compromised.
requirements: New setting `ALLOWED_OPERATION_TYPES` (comma separated, for example `setOptions,bumpSequence`)
If set, a transaction with any other operation type is refused with `400`
If unset, behaviour does not change
The refusal message names the rejected type
Document the trade-offs in the README
execution: Extend `parseAndValidate` in `src/signing/validate.ts` and pass the policy from `src/config.ts`.
tests: Add cases to `test/validate.test.ts` for allowed, refused and unset. Commit: `feat(signing): add operation allow list`.

title: feat(signing): add an optional time bounds requirement
description: A signed transaction with no expiry can be used much later. Operators may want to require time bounds.
requirements: New settings `REQUIRE_TIME_BOUNDS` and `MAX_TX_VALIDITY_SECONDS`
When enabled, refuse transactions with no `maxTime`, or with a `maxTime` further away than the limit
Default is off, so current behaviour does not change
Clear `400` messages
Document how wallets should set time bounds when building recovery transactions
execution: Time bounds are on the parsed transaction (`tx.timeBounds`). Handle the case where it is undefined.
tests: Tests for missing, too far, and acceptable time bounds. Commit: `feat(signing): add time bounds policy`.

title: feat(auth): support muxed account SEP-10 subjects
description: SEP-10 tokens may identify a muxed account (an `M...` address). `sep10Principal` accepts only `G...` addresses, so those tokens are refused.
requirements: Check the current SEP-10 text for how muxed subjects are formatted, and link it in the pull request
Accept a muxed subject and map it to its base `G...` account
Keep refusing malformed subjects
Do not let a memo or muxed id widen access to other accounts
Document the behaviour
execution: The SDK can decode muxed addresses. Add the cases to `src/auth/authenticator.ts`.
tests: Tests in a new `test/authenticator.test.ts` for `G`, `G:memo`, `M` and malformed subjects. Commit: `feat(auth): support muxed subjects`.

title: fix(security): harden HTTP defaults
description: The server uses Fastify defaults. A recovery server should be stricter about headers, timeouts and proxies.
requirements: Add security headers (for example `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Cache-Control: no-store` on all account responses)
Set connection, request and keep-alive timeouts
Add a `TRUST_PROXY` setting so client IPs are right behind a load balancer, default off
Reject requests with a body on `GET` and `DELETE`
Document each setting
execution: Use Fastify hooks in `src/api/server.ts`. Avoid adding a large dependency for a few headers.
tests: Tests that the headers are present and that timeouts are configured. Commit: `fix(security): harden http defaults`.

title: ci: add Dependabot and an npm audit job
description: Dependencies are not updated or checked automatically. A key-holding service should not fall behind on security fixes.
requirements: Add `.github/dependabot.yml` for npm and GitHub Actions, weekly
Add a CI job that runs `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`
The job must not block pull requests on unrelated advisories forever: document how to handle a known false positive
execution: Keep the new job separate from the `test` job so branch protection on `test` is unchanged.
tests: Show the job running in the pull request. Commit: `ci: add dependabot and audit job`.

title: docs: write an OpenAPI description of the six endpoints
description: Wallet developers want a machine readable description of the API.
requirements: `docs/openapi.yaml` (OpenAPI 3) covering all six SEP-30 endpoints and `/healthz`
Request and response bodies, status codes and the two authentication styles
A test that fails if a route in `src/api/server.ts` is missing from the file, or the reverse
Linked from the README
execution: Describe what the code does today and check it against the SEP-30 text.
tests: The route-matching test is the proof. Commit: `docs: add openapi description`.

title: docs: write an operator guide for running two independent servers
description: The security of SEP-30 depends on servers being run by different parties. Operators need a clear guide.
requirements: `docs/operator-guide.md` covering configuration, key encryption key backup and restore, and upgrades
A section on why two containers you control are not independent, and what independence means in practice
How to set account thresholds and signer weights so no single server can act, with a testnet walkthrough that you have actually run
How to check the result with `lumenward-audit`
What to do if a server is lost or compromised
execution: Run every command you document on testnet and paste real output.
tests: Docs only. Commit: `docs: add operator guide`.

title: docs: write a wallet integration guide
description: Wallet developers need to know how to enrol an account and run a recovery against Lumenward.
requirements: `docs/wallet-guide.md` with a worked TypeScript example: SEP-10 login, register, add signers, recover
Use the official wallet SDK where it supports the step, and say where it does not
Explain identity choices and their risks
Verify the example runs against a local Lumenward on testnet and say which SDK version you used
execution: Check the SDK's current documentation first, because its API changes between versions.
tests: Docs only, but include a runnable example under `examples/`. Commit: `docs: add wallet integration guide`.
